subject: Helia discovery: eval recommendations, model snapshot & rollback proposal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@helia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + evaluation artifacts from today's discovery

Ellie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate:

Summary of needs (from call)
- High-throughput classification and entity extraction for financial docs (monthly statements, invoices).
- Strong determinism on numeric outputs and minimal hallucination around balances and dates.
- Data residency: US-only processing; evidence of audit logs is required for procurement.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we'll deliver)
1) Eval pack (attached): benchmark scripts, golden test set (200 samples), and prompt variants specific to invoice/statement formatting.
2) Two candidate model configurations to test:
   - rw-infer-v1.3 (Redwood-optimized Llama-variant, float16 + KV-cache improvements) — baseline for latency/cost.
   - Llama-2-13B-q4f32 (quantized) — higher determinism on structured outputs in our past tests.
3) Pin policy suggestion: snapshot rw-infer-v1.3@2026-09-29 for initial trial and gate any rollout to later versions behind a canary with golden-set pass rate >= 98%.

Links and artifacts (also attached)
- Eval pack: helia-eval-pack-v1.zip (contains prompts, scripts)
- Benchmark summary: redwood-benchmarks-202610.pdf
- Quick runbook for snapshot/pin: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Helia/HL-4392/eval-pack

Asks / next steps
- Can you upload a small redacted sample of 50 documents (in the attached CSV format) so we can run the golden-set locally? (Devon / Ellie)
- I'll loop in Marissa on the specific eval thresholds and a timeline for a 2-week trial.

Timing: we can turn on a sandbox eval in 48–72 hours once we have the sample. If you want, we can pre-snapshot rw-infer-v1.3 so we have a rollback point ready.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment stubs: helia-eval-pack-v1.zip (zip), helia-sample-prompts.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ellie Park <ellie@helia.ai>, Devon Li <devon.li@helia.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + evaluation artifacts from today's discovery

Sean / Ellie / Devon — added a couple technical clarifications after reviewing the call notes: 

1) Eval thresholds- we recommend the following pass gates for the golden set to consider a model "fit":
   - Entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on invoice IDs / dates
   - Numeric exact-match for balances >= 0.985 (we strip punctuation/formatting before compare)
   - No hallucination/false-positive rate on blank fields > 0.02

2) Suggested prompt families (in the CSV): structured prompt, instruction-only, and delimiter-enhanced templates. We'll run all three families in parallel and include aggregate metrics.

3) On pinning/rollback: Grace will own the snapshot policy if Helia asks for a pinned deployment. Process we propose:
   - Snapshot current model binary + config (immutable tag)
   - Expose read-only inference endpoint for Helia's sandbox pinned to that snapshot
   - Gate production promotion behind the golden-set pass and a 24-hour canary monitoring window (telemetry hooks will be provided)

4) Security/compliance note: we'll provide the audit log sample export for the procurement questionnaire. Expect a DOCX with sample events by EOD tomorrow.

I'll prepare a short acceptance checklist for the golden-set so the Helia team knows what "pass" looks like. Sean — if you can confirm the 50-sample ETA that helps us prioritize.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment stubs referenced: redwood-goldenset-checklist.md (md), audit-log-sample.docx (docx)

From: Ellie Park <ellie@helia.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@helia.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + evaluation artifacts from today's discovery

Thanks — this is helpful and thorough. We'll get the 50 redacted docs back to you by tomorrow morning. Couple of datapoints from our side to call out:

- We recently ran a small internal test against the public Llama-2-13B and saw a recurring problem where the model occasionally invents vendor names for partially redacted invoices (e.g., producing "Northgate Supplies" when the vendor field was missing).
- Our procurement team will need the audit-log sample and the SOC2 questionnaire answers before we can move forward on PO paperwork.

Two asks from Helia:
1) If we find a regression after you upgrade our pinned model (e.g., rw-infer-v1.3 -> rw-infer-v1.4), will we be able to automatically roll back to the last snapshot? What does that timeline look like?
2) Can you include a small section in the runbook on how to interpret token-level cost spikes if we see them in the canary window?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Devon and I will upload the sample CSV to the Drive link and tag you.

—Ellie
Head of Product | Helia.ai
ellie@helia.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@helia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + evaluation artifacts from today's discovery

Ellie / Devon — great questions. Short answers and proposed operational commitments below so procurement has something to sign off on quickly.

1) Rollback/rollback timeline
   - Yes. We will pin a snapshot (immutable tag) for Helia's sandbox. If a regression is detected after a subsequent upgrade, we can revert the sandbox endpoint to the pinned snapshot within 15 minutes. For production rollbacks we target 30–60 minutes depending on traffic and any in-flight requests; we'll perform the rollback and verify golden-set metrics within the 1-hour window.

2) Automated safeguards
   - Canary policy we will configure: 1% of production traffic (or a fixed 5 r/s) for 24 hours with automated alerting if golden-set pass rate falls below thresholds or token-cost-per-request increases by > 25% vs baseline.
   - If alerts fire, the system will automatically pause the rollout and route traffic back to the pinned snapshot pending human review.

3) Runbook updates
   - We'll add a short section on interpreting per-token cost spikes (debugging steps, where to look in the Console traces, typical causes such as runaway sampling temperature or prompt injection). Marissa will draft the FAQ entry.

Procurement note: we'll attach the audit-log sample and a SOC2 summary by EOD for your procurement team. I'll also add a short paragraph to the HubSpot deal record summarizing the rollback SLA commitments so it shows up for procurement reviewers.

Next steps
- Helia: upload CSV sample to the Drive link (once done, reply-all).
- Redwood: we snapshot rw-infer-v1.3@2026-09-29 and prepare the sandbox pinned endpoint. Marissa will publish the golden-set checklist.

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical alignment next Wednesday so Grace and Marissa can walk the Helia engineers through the runbook and cost telemetry.

Thanks —
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192
